input_oneliner: 81F on sotalol for AF, found on floor by bed, no memory of event, no prodrome, tele leads off at the time, K 3.1 this AM

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about prodrome (none vs palpitations vs lightheadedness), what she was doing (lying vs standing), and duration of unconsciousness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Absent prodrome and supine onset favor arrhythmia

reference_targets_freetext.item: Witness account: duration, color, jerking, tongue biting, incontinence, post-event confusion (from nurse)
Medication review (MAR): sotalol dose and timing, other QT-prolonging or AV-nodal agents, recent additions
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Sotalol with hypokalemia is a torsades set-up; AV-nodal agents cause bradyarrhythmia; indispensable here, likely maps to a not_quantified record

reference_targets_freetext.item: Orthostatic vital signs (supine to standing at 1 and 3 min)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Excludes an orthostatic contribution in an elderly inpatient

reference_targets_freetext.item: Examine for injury (scalp, face, hip) from an unheralded fall
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Injury without protective response suggests abrupt arrhythmic loss of consciousness

reference_targets_freetext.item: Cardiac exam: heart rate, rhythm regularity, and murmur
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Detects bradycardia, irregular rhythm, or a structural clue

should_not_recommend: Carotid sinus massage in a patient on sotalol with suspected conduction disease
Attribute to dehydration and remove from telemetry
